papers.title: Romantic Attachment and Controlling Behaviors in Adolescent Dating Relationships: Indirect Links Through Relational Skills.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Controlling behaviors (i.e., exerting power over a partner's thoughts, feelings, or behaviors) are a form of teen dating violence (TDV) that can have significant psychological and relational consequences. Although insecure romantic attachment is one of the main risk factors associated with TDV perpetration, no study has specifically examined its links with controlling behaviors in adolescence. Furthermore, the mechanisms that may explain this association have yet to be examined. Since romantic attachment serves as a foundation for the development of relational skills (individuality, assertiveness, support), these skills may play a role in the perpetration of controlling behaviors among adolescents with attachment insecurities in romantic contexts. This study examined the relationship between attachment anxiety and avoidance and the perpetration of controlling behaviors via these three forms of relational skills. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, a sample of 361 Canadian adolescents (Mage = 17.21, SD = 1.22) currently in a dating relationship completed an online questionnaire between 2022 and 2024. RESULTS: Path analyses revealed an indirect association between attachment anxiety and the perpetration of controlling behaviors via lower individuality. The results also indicated an indirect association between attachment avoidance and controlling behaviors via lower support offered. The model explains 16.5% of the variance in the perpetration of controlling behaviors. CONCLUSION: This study highlights the relevance of romantic attachment and relationship skills in understanding controlling behaviors in teen dating relationships and suggests that prevention programs may benefit from targeting relational skills, especially among adolescents with attachment insecurity.

papers.title: Reliability of a functional electromechanical dynamometer for a bilateral standing press exercise at intensities of 30% and 60% of isometric peak force in trained women.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Determining the reliability of exercise instruments and protocols in the fields of health and sports performance is of great interest due to their close relationship with monitoring and decision-making in athletes. Studies in trained women are limited, and more evidence is needed on performance variables and the reliability of exercise protocols. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the reliability of an exercise protocol for determining mean muscle strength, mean velocity, and mean power during the bilateral standing press (BSP) in trained women. METHODS: Sixteen trained women (age = 20.0 ± 2.30 years; body mass = 67.63 ± 6.68 kg; height = 1.65 ± 0.06 m) participated in this repeated-measures study. Absolute reliability was assessed using the coefficient of variation (CV), and relative reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for a bilateral standing press (BSP) exercise protocol performed at intensities of 30% and 60% of isometric peak force (IPF). RESULTS: Mean muscle strength showed acceptable absolute reliability and extremely high relative reliability at both 30% IPF (CV = 6.51%; ICC = 0.94) and 60% IPF (CV = 5.03%; ICC = 0.97). Mean velocity showed extremely high relative reliability at 60% IPF (ICC = 0.92), but its absolute reliability was not acceptable at either 30% IPF (CV = 10.10%; ICC = 0.75) or 60% IPF (CV = 14.16%; ICC = 0.92). Mean power also exceeded the predefined CV threshold at 30% IPF (CV = 11.16%; ICC = 0.85) and at 60% IPF (CV = 14.35%; ICC = 0.89). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that the BSP protocol using functional electromechanical dynamometry is reliable for assessing mean muscle strength in trained women. However, mean velocity and mean power should be interpreted with caution, as their absolute reliability did not reach the predefined threshold of acceptable reliability.

papers.title: Intraparotid lipoma in a 15-year-old girl: MRI-based diagnosis of a rare parotid lesion.
papers.abstract: Intraparotid lipoma is a rare benign tumor of the parotid gland, accounting for less than 1% of all parotid tumors. Its slow growth and typically painless presentation often lead to delayed diagnosis, which relies primarily on imaging findings. We report the case of a 15-year-old girl presenting with a painless left cheek swelling, evolving since the age of five and causing progressive discomfort, without any associated clinical signs. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated the typical features of an intraparotid lipoma, including high signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images, complete signal suppression on fat-saturated sequences, and no significant enhancement following gadolinium administration, supporting a highly confident non-invasive diagnosis. This case highlights the value of MRI in characterizing a fatty parotid lesion and establishing a confident non-invasive diagnosis in an adolescent patient, potentially avoiding unnecessary invasive procedures, particularly in an anatomically complex region due to the close relationship between the parotid gland and the facial nerve.

papers.title: Smart Molecular Crystals With Dynamic Photonic Modulation and Integrated Waveguiding.
papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive materials capable of dynamically tuning their optical outputs promise new architectures for smart photonics, yet simultaneously achieving rapid response kinetics and low loss optical waveguiding within a single crystal phase remains challenging. Here, we present two Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) active Schiff base crystals where supramolecular hydrogen bonding engineering resolves this trade-off. By strategically introducing intermolecular hydrogen bonding networks alongside intrinsic intramolecular proton transfer channels, these crystals deliver highly sensitive, fully reversible thermofluorochromic switching coupled with efficient waveguiding performance. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and theoretical calculations reveal that the subtle interplay between molecular conformation and supramolecular packing topology governs both the thermal emission color gradation and the quenching dynamics. Leveraging these dual photonic functions, we demonstrate a multilevel anti-counterfeiting platform that pairs static visual features with dynamic thermal responsiveness. Overall, this work highlights the potential of tailor-made supramolecular architectures in converting organic molecular crystals into versatile building blocks for advanced micro-/nanophotonics and information encryption.

papers.title: Preliminary Evaluation of Implementation and Effectiveness of the Relational Suicide Intervention Pilot.
papers.abstract: Although primary interventions for suicidal ideation typically focus on individuals, couple-based clinical interventions for this population remain underdeveloped. Despite emerging evidence suggesting that relational interventions may improve suicidal ideation, currently only one couple-based intervention has preliminary evidence, and it was specifically designed for military couples. This gap highlights the need for systemic couple-based interventions in outpatient settings. We piloted the Relational Suicide Intervention (RSI), a four-session intervention grounded in Integrative Systemic Therapy and contemporary suicidology research, at a university clinic. Sixteen graduate student therapists consented to participate and received training in the intervention. Of four couples screened, three met eligibility criteria, consented, and completed the study. We used a mixed-methods approach to evaluate qualitative and quantitative data. Findings provided preliminary support for the safe and feasible implementation of RSI in this small pilot sample. Relationship satisfaction showed small average increases, particularly among partners with higher suicidal ideation, whereas suicidal ideation did not improve on average. Participants generally described the intervention as helpful, particularly regarding suicide safety planning, understanding relationship patterns, and learning mental health coping strategies. These preliminary findings suggest promise for RSI, with future research needed to replicate findings with larger samples, diverse clinical settings, and longer treatment durations comparable to traditional couple therapy.
